w: Built by the Spanish between 1577 and 1604 on the Pic d'Aidour, 400 metres above the Gulf of Oran, one of three Oran forts once linked by tunnels. The French took it in 1831. A chapel below carries a giant Virgin Mary statue, styled Notre-Dame du Salut de Santa Cruz after Marseille's basilica.

w: Once the Grande Synagogue d'Oran, the largest synagogue in Africa, also known as Temple Israelite, standing on what is now Boulevard Maata Mohamed El Habib. It served Oran's Jewish community before being repurposed, and today is the Abdellah Ben Salem Mosque.
s: Africa's largest synagogue, now a mosque

w: Also called the Suicide Charge at Oran, this Allied operation was part of Operation Torch, the invasion of North Africa. Rather than landing on the surrounding beaches, troops tried to force their way directly into Oran's harbour, an exposed manoeuvre that gave the raid its grim nickname.
s: Suicide Charge at Oran, a 1942 harbour raid

w: In the 1980s Bishop Pierre Claverie handed this newer, much larger cathedral over to the Algerian authorities, and Oran's Catholic seat moved instead into the crypt of the older Church of St Mary. Sacre-Coeur stands at Place de la Kahina, now a former Catholic church rather than an active cathedral.
s: Oran's larger cathedral, later handed over

w: Completed in 2015 and named for Abdelhamid Ben Badis, a figure revered among Algerian Muslims. In 1931 Ben Badis helped found the Association of Algerian Muslim Ulema, an Islamic reformist organisation that fought assimilation into colonial French culture. This Sunni mosque carries his name and legacy.
s: Named for Algeria's reformist imam, Ben Badis

w: An 18th-century Ottoman palace built for Muhammad Bey the Great, seat of the rulers of the Western Baylik, near Mount Marjaju in the Sidi al-Houari quarter. Its 5.6 hectares hold a diwan, a harem, barracks used as stables by both Ottomans and French, and two guard towers dating to 1345. Now a national heritage site.

Seat of the Western Baylik's rulers

w: Named for Ahmed Zabana, the Algerian national hero executed by the French on 19 May 1956 in Algiers, in the opening months of the war of independence. Oran's national museum has carried his name ever since, a permanent civic memorial folded into the city's main museum building rather than set apart as its own monument.
s: Named for an executed independence hero

w: A colonial-era hotel dated to 1920, once among the most luxurious in Oran, with 112 rooms, 12 junior suites and five senior suites. Now run by Accor under its MGallery Hotel Collection, the building keeps its early-twentieth-century grandeur behind a modern hospitality brand, a survivor of French Oran's hotel boom.
s: 1920s colonial hotel, now run by Accor

w: Built in the 1960s in the Saint-Eugene quarter to replace an earlier, unfinished church, St Mary's served as the parish church of its neighbourhood. When the larger Sacred Heart Cathedral was handed to the Algerian authorities in the 1980s, the bishop's seat moved here instead. It was fully renovated in 2012.
